name: Contract requirement return types reflect as normalized Types

input.source_text: contract Numbers for Iterable<Integer> { fun iterator() -> Iterator<Integer> } [Numbers.requirement(:iterator).return_type, Iterator<Integer>.requirement(:next).return_type, Iterator<Integer>.requirement(:close).return_type]

applicability.reason: Requires built-in Iterable/Iterator/Iteration names, generic `extends`, and requirement reflection. The row's own source writes `contract Numbers for Iterable<Integer>`, which is ungrammatical: `contract_decl` fixes the only Contract inheritance clause as `extends`, and `for` is the CLASS conformance keyword. That contradiction is recorded in docs/spec-defects-v1.md - V350 is the only place in the spec writing it, and D-466, the decision it cites, spells the same Contracts with no `for` at all - so the implementation keeps `extends`. Correcting the spelling alone does not make the row observable: `Iterable`, `Iterator` and `Iteration` do not resolve as names, `extends Base<Integer>` with a type ARGUMENT is refused, and `Contract.requirement(:sel).return_type` does not exist.

expect.status: Compilation succeeds and the exact normalized Types are [Iterator<Integer>, Iteration<Integer>, Nil].
